name: Qwen3.5-0.8B-weight-space-programming
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B (config.json max_position_embeddings 262144). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: hybrid: Gated DeltaNet linear attention with full gated attention every 4th layer (6 of 24)
notes: ADDED 2026-11-08 from the trending feed (2,774 downloads, 122 likes, repo created 2026-11-02). NOT a finetune in the usual sense and derivative_kind is set to 'other' for that reason: there is no gradient descent, no training run and no preference optimisation. A frontier LLM ('Astra', driven through Hugging Face's ML Intern) was given a Python session over the weights and 50 forward passes on GSM8K/MATH training problems, and it subtracted one 'thinking-loop' direction - traced to layers 15 and 19 - from 64 output columns of down_proj in each of those two layers: 131,072 weights, 0.016% of the model. The tool's default 'finetune' label would have misdescribed the method. VERIFIABILITY: this is the best-verified edit in the catalog. The delta is published as a bit-exact diff (RikiyaT/lm_understand-logs, exp8_math/runs/p50c/edit/), the checkpoint was rebuilt with exp8_math/code/apply_edit.py which sha256-checks every rebuilt tensor against the evaluated checkpoint, and the card prints the sha256 of BOTH changed tensors (layers.15.mlp.down_proj.weight 82e2d733..., layers.19.mlp.down_proj.weight 8ef3c61b...). Only those two tensors differ from Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B at 2fc06364715b967f1860aea9cf38778875588b17. ARCHITECTURE/MEMORY: inherited unchanged from models/qwen3-5-0-8b - 24 layers, hybrid Gated DeltaNet with full attention every 4th layer (6 of 24), hidden 1024, 8 query / 2 KV heads, head_dim 256, 262144 context, 12,288 B/token KV (6 full-attention layers x 2 x 2 x 256 x 2 B; the 18 linear layers hold constant state). PARAMS 0.873B, dense, so active_params_b = params_b. HARDWARE GATE: passes trivially - 0.873B active (<= 40) and 0.873 x 0.5 = 0.44 GiB at the 4-bit planning figure (<= 128); the card also gives 51 min for 2,000 generations x 32k tokens on a single H200, i.e. it runs on one consumer-class GPU at far smaller batch. WHAT IT WINS: everything on the card, and by an implausible-looking margin that the independent re-run supports - MATH-500 48.1 against the base's 7.9 in the same table (51.0 on a full 500x4 re-run vs the base's 5.0 on a 25-problem smoke test), GSM8K 67.1 vs 13.8, IFEval 62.3 vs 21.0, and answers hitting the token limit 33.1% vs 93.0%. The mechanism is stated and matches the numbers: the base loops on math until the budget runs out. WHAT IT LOSES / CAVEATS, all from the card: (1) 7.9 on MATH-500 is a LOW base - the 0.8B is weak at math to begin with, so a large ratio is not a large capability; 48-51% MATH-500 at 0.873B is still well under any 4B model in the catalog. (2) The headline table's several-samples-per-problem protocol is the authors', not a standard harness, and it is not the same as the 4-sample re-run - the two numbers (48.1, 51.0) must not be averaged. (3) GSM8K and IFEval have no independent re-run; only MATH-500 does. (4) This is a single published experiment (Experiment 8 of the 'Sparks of Weight-Space Programming' post), n=1 in the sense of one checkpoint and one method trial - the result says an LLM with a weight-editing session CAN find a real direction in a small model, not that the technique is reliable. benchmarks.name: MATH-500
benchmarks.config: Card 'Results' table, row 'Edited (this model)' 48.1 vs row 'Base' 7.9, SAME table, same protocol (thinking on, up to 32,768 tokens, several samples per problem, the post's own harness). Vendor claim. INDEPENDENT RE-RUN on the card corroborates it and is the stronger number on this record: 51.0% over the full 500 problems x 4 samples = 2,000 generations, vLLM 0.33.0, temp 0.6, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, presence_penalty 1.5, max 32,768 new tokens, seed 0, last \boxed{} graded with math-verify 0.9.0, 51 min on one H200; the base scored 5.0% on a 25-problem smoke test with 95% hitting the token limit. Per-problem results shipped in eval/. The 48.1 row is recorded as the score because it is the card's headline table; the 51.0 re-run is the number to quote when asked whether it replicates.

benchmarks.name: GSM8K
benchmarks.config: Same card table: Edited 67.1 vs Base 13.8. Same protocol as the MATH-500 row. No independent re-run published for GSM8K - only MATH-500 was re-run.

benchmarks.name: IFEval
benchmarks.config: Same card table: Edited 62.3 vs Base 21.0. This is the row that shows the edit was not purely a math patch: instruction following nearly tripled, which the card attributes to the model no longer looping to the token limit rather than to any IF-specific training.

benchmarks.name: Hit token limit (%, lower is better)
benchmarks.config: Same card table: Edited 33.1 vs Base 93.0. LOWER IS BETTER - the schema's higher_is_better is set false. This is the mechanism behind all three rows above: the base answers loop until the budget runs out on 93% of math problems, the edit cuts that to a third. The independent re-run measured 31.6% on the edited checkpoint and 95% for the base on a 25-problem smoke test, consistent with this row.
